From 854f32648b8a5e424d682953b1a9f3b7c3322701 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Liang Wang <wangliang101@huawei.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2021 16:54:45 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] lib: use PFN_PHYS() in devmem_is_allowed()

The physical address may exceed 32 bits on 32-bit systems with more than
32 bits of physcial address.  Use PFN_PHYS() in devmem_is_allowed(), or
the physical address may overflow and be truncated.

We found this bug when mapping a high addresses through devmem tool,
when CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM is enabled on the ARM with ARM_LPAE and devmem
is used to map a high address that is not in the iomem address range, an
unexpected error indicating no permission is returned.

This bug was initially introduced from v2.6.37, and the function was
moved to lib in v5.11.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20210731025057.78825-1-wangliang101@huawei.com
Fixes: 087aaffcdf9c ("ARM: implement CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM by disabling access to RAM via /dev/mem")
Fixes: 527701eda5f1 ("lib: Add a generic version of devmem_is_allowed()")
Signed-off-by: Liang Wang <wangliang101@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: Luis Chamberlain <mcgrof@kernel.org>
Cc: Palmer Dabbelt <palmerdabbelt@google.com>
Cc: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Cc: Russell King <linux@armlinux.org.uk>
Cc: Liang Wang <wangliang101@huawei.com>
Cc: Xiaoming Ni <nixiaoming@huawei.com>
Cc: Kefeng Wang <wangkefeng.wang@huawei.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>	[2.6.37+]
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/lib/devmem_is_allowed.c b/lib/devmem_is_allowed.c
index c0d67c541849..60be9e24bd57 100644
--- a/lib/devmem_is_allowed.c
+++ b/lib/devmem_is_allowed.c
@@ -19,7 +19,7 @@
  */
 int devmem_is_allowed(unsigned long pfn)
 {
-	if (iomem_is_exclusive(pfn << PAGE_SHIFT))
+	if (iomem_is_exclusive(PFN_PHYS(pfn)))
 		return 0;
 	if (!page_is_ram(pfn))
 		return 1;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `lib/devmem_is_allowed.c`**
   - The line of code that checks if the physical frame number (PFN) is exclusive to I/O memory has been modified. 
   - The original code used `iomem_is_exclusive(pfn << PAGE_SHIFT)`, which shifts the PFN by the page shift amount to convert it to a physical address.
   - The modified code uses `iomem_is_exclusive(PFN_PHYS(pfn))`, which directly converts the PFN to a physical address using the `PFN_PHYS()` macro, ensuring that the physical address is correctly calculated and preventing potential overflow issues.

### Relationships

- The modification in `lib/devmem_is_allowed.c` addresses a bug related to handling physical addresses that may exceed 32 bits on 32-bit systems. 
- The change is crucial for maintaining the integrity of memory access checks when the `CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM` option is enabled, particularly in scenarios involving high physical addresses on ARM architectures with large physical address extensions (ARM_LPAE).
- This patch is a fix for a previously introduced bug from version v2.6.37, which was exacerbated when the function was moved to the `lib` directory in v5.11. The use of `PFN_PHYS()` ensures that the physical address calculations are accurate, thus preventing unexpected permission errors when accessing memory through the `/dev/mem` interface.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (iomem_is_exclusive(pfn << PAGE_SHIFT))
```
Reason:
The left shift operation (`pfn << PAGE_SHIFT`) is used to convert the page frame number (PFN) to a physical address. On 32-bit systems with more than 32 bits of physical address space, this operation can cause overflow and truncation of the address, leading to incorrect permission checks and unexpected errors when accessing high memory addresses.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (iomem_is_exclusive(PFN_PHYS(pfn)))
```
Reason:
The use of `PFN_PHYS(pfn)` correctly converts the PFN to a physical address without the risk of overflow, ensuring that the permission checks are accurate for high memory addresses. This change prevents the erroneous behavior that occurs when the physical address exceeds the 32-bit limit.
